summary: The menu is dated 2026-11-17, not today, and every candidate's F-score is fully computable (fscore_computable 9), so I rank on in-sector gross profitability and on cash flow backing earnings. VRSN, CARG and FTDR lead, with DPZ, TPR, IDXX and SAM next. Most of the menu's leaders are already held; FTDR and TPR are the strongest names not held. No lesson in learning.json names the fundamentals-analyst and I have no graded calls yet, so none shaped this ranking. I used news_memory and the lesson evidence only to keep deal-pending names (CART, RRC) out of the ranking.

rankings.why: The only 9/9 F-score with gp_sector_pct 0.993 (gross profitability 1.10). CFO of $1.09B covers net income of $826M. All nine tests pass, including leverage_not_up and no_dilution. Held.
rankings.concerns: FY ended 2025-12-31, so these numbers are almost 11 months old. The FY2026 10-K should arrive around February.

rankings.why: gp_sector_pct 1.0 (gross profitability 1.27), F8. CFO of $295M is nearly double net income of $156M, the strongest cash backing among the top names. Its only failed test is current_ratio_improved. Held.
rankings.concerns: vol_252d of 0.406 is close to the 0.443 cutoff. The Technology label is loose for an auto marketplace, but the SIC (computer processing) supports it.

rankings.why: F9 with all nine tests passing and gp_sector_pct 0.954. CFO of $416M against net income of $255M. Not held, so it is the best unheld name on the numbers.
rankings.concerns: An 8-K 5.02 filed 11-12 is still unread per news_memory (11-17); check it before any proposal. vol_252d 0.421 is near the cutoff.

rankings.why: Gross profitability 1.15, F8. CFO of $792M covers net income of $602M. Every test passes except leverage_not_up. Held.
rankings.concerns: The gp_sector_pct of 1.0 is ranked against Consumer Staples through a wholesale-groceries SIC. DPZ is a restaurant franchisor, so the top-of-sector rank is an artifact and the case rests on absolute quality only. Leverage rose.

rankings.why: F8, gp_sector_pct 0.943. CFO of $1.98B against net income of $1.53B. Its fiscal year is fresh (fy_end 2026-06-27). Its only failed test is current_ratio_improved. Not held.
rankings.concerns: vol_252d 0.407. Per news_memory, several PT cuts came before its 11-05 print. That is a sentiment note, not an accounting one.

rankings.why: F8, gp_sector_pct 0.942. CFO of $1.18B is above net income of $1.06B. Its only failed test is current_ratio_improved. Held.
rankings.concerns: Cash backing is thinner here than for the names above (CFO only modestly above net income). It sits in the Health Care sleeve alongside INCY and EXEL.

rankings.why: F8, gp_sector_pct 0.945. CFO of $270M is about 2.5x net income of $108M, which is strong cash backing. Held since 11-17.
rankings.concerns: Net income is small against $1.96B of revenue, so profitability depends on gross margin holding (gross_margin_improved passes).

rankings.why: F9 with all tests passing, and the freshest annual data on the menu (fy_end 2026-09-26, known since 2026-11-03). CFO of $145.1B is above net income of $132.2B. gp_sector_pct 0.892. Not held.
rankings.concerns: Its in-sector percentile is lower than the leaders'. Per news_memory, a memory-cost margin warning came in early November, and the 10-K numbers may not show that yet.

rankings.why: F8, gp_sector_pct 0.905. CFO of $1.41B covers net income of $1.29B. Both leverage_not_up and current_ratio_improved pass. Held.
rankings.concerns: The MAESTRA-3 Phase 3 cancellation (11-16, guidance kept) is a pipeline point the 10-K does not capture. It overlaps EXEL in the oncology sleeve.

rankings.why: F9 with all tests passing. CFO of $584M is well above net income of $344M. Low vol (0.326). Not held, and in Communication, a sector the book does not hold by label.
rankings.concerns: Its gp_sector_pct of 0.833 is the lowest in this list. FY ended 2025-12-31.

red_flags.flag: CFO of $114M is barely over half of net income ($204M), and the cfo_exceeds_net_income test fails. This is the largest accrual gap on the menu.

Its flags show an amended 10-K/10-Q in the last two years (possible restatement), and CFO ($1.633B) is below net income ($1.664B). Two separate concerns on one name. The Industrials label also understates its consumer-electronics exposure.
Its flags show an amended 10-K/10-Q in the last two years (possible restatement). It also fails both leverage_not_up and no_dilution.
Stale data: fy_end 2025-06-30, known since 2025-08-08. The FY2026 10-K (year ending June 2026) should have been filed by now, so the screen is scoring numbers more than 16 months old.
Old data: fy_end 2025-09-30, known since 2025-11-25. It reported fiscal Q4 on 11-04 per news_memory, so a new 10-K is due and these numbers are about to be replaced. It also fails no_dilution.
Old data: fy_end 2025-09-27, known since 2025-11-24, with an FY2026 10-K due. Its 8-K 5.02 from 11-10 aged out of the window unread.

Pending acquisition by DoorDash at $65 (8-K 1.01, 10-29), now under DOJ antitrust review (11-17). The fundamentals are irrelevant to a deal-spread position, so I leave it out of the ranking. The Industrials label also doesn't fit a grocery-delivery platform.
Subject to the EQT all-stock acquisition (8-K 1.01, 10-26). Its gp_sector_pct of 1.0 no longer describes a standalone investment. Left out of the ranking.
CFO ($755M) is slightly below net income ($765M), and cfo_exceeds_net_income fails.

Its Industrials label is an SIC artifact for a financial-data business. It fails leverage_not_up, which it shares with MCO (also mislabelled Industrials), so the held financial-data sleeve has rising leverage in both names.
A credit-ratings business labelled Industrials. It fails leverage_not_up and has the lowest gp_sector_pct (0.825) of any held name on the menu.
Labelled Consumer Discretionary (building-materials retail SIC), but it is an industrial MRO distributor, so its 0.873 percentile is measured against the wrong peers. MSM carries the same mislabel.
Its gross profitability of 3.33 rests on a very small asset base ($24.9M of total assets) for a franchisor, so its 1.0 percentile overstates its quality relative to peers. It also fails no_dilution.

Labelled Consumer Staples (drug-store SIC), but most of the business is insurance and PBM. Net income of $1.77B on $402B of revenue is very thin, though CFO of $10.6B backs it. Fails roa_improved and no_dilution.
A lighting maker labelled Technology. HWM (aerospace components) is labelled Materials. Both percentiles are measured against mismatched peers.

holdings_notes.note: An S&P 500 ETF. It can never pass a single-stock SEC screen, so being off the menu is structural and not a fundamentals signal. Review it on its own invalidation (the SPY 200-day line it shares with VTI), not on this menu.
Same as VOO: a broad-market ETF outside the screen's scope. Being off the menu says nothing new. It shares VOO's stop, so it should be judged with VOO as one position.

Every held single stock is still on the 11-17 menu: VRSN, CARG, DPZ, IDXX, SAM, INCY, EXEL, MSCI, MCO, FAST, KR and WMT. None fell off the screen, so no 'screen drops it' clause trips on this menu. WMT reports today (11-19), and its FY2026-01 numbers will be superseded at its next 10-K, not by today's quarterly print.
